owner_statement:
D-P4.6-PLAN-AUTH: I, mayank-admin, authorize planning, read-only repository analysis, and official primary-source research only for P4.6 Operations, Security, And Scale.

The authorized planning scope includes local documentation for platform-wide low-cardinality metrics; trace and correlation-context propagation; separation of operational logs, security logs, audit records, and evidence records; sanitized failure taxonomy; service-level indicators, service-level objectives, error budgets, alert thresholds, and degradation states; queue leases, retries, backoff, dead-letter handling, circuit breakers, idempotency, graceful shutdown, kill switches, and abandoned-work recovery; application authorization and PostgreSQL row-security equivalence; department isolation, privileged-role misuse, cross-scope denial, adversarial-input, and abuse testing; dependency, artifact, license, SBOM, vulnerability, provenance, and supply-chain controls; backup, restore, disaster-recovery, RPO/RTO, and recovery-drill design; dynamic hardware capability profiles; standalone, GPU-lab, server, and Kubernetes topology planning without execution; generated-only C1/C10/C50 capacity methodology covering latency, throughput, backlog, saturation, recovery, resource use, and declared hardware limitations; non-effective owner decision options; and a bounded P4.6 implementation plan and planning package.

Internet research is limited to official primary technical, security, reliability, database, observability, supply-chain, container, Kubernetes, and standards sources. Local planning documentation, validation, and one checkpoint commit without push are authorized.

This does not authorize product, test, migration, dependency, container, Kubernetes, deployment, or runtime implementation; process, service, container, cluster, backup, restore, scanner, hardware, performance, stress, or recovery execution; installation, update, download, or artifact acquisition; credentials or secrets; provider, Sentinel, camera, media, or operational network access; Government, police, private, biometric, owner, registration, watchlist, case, or evidence data; models, datasets, inference, or training; operational alerts, notifications, dispatch, enforcement, or autonomous actions; production or pilot deployment; or push, pull, fetch, pull request, merge, release, or other remote Git activity.
